A1.justification: Despite the Bone-to-DiSHA reframing, the shared methods, experiments and retained results establish that these are versions of the same work. Both PDFs are readable throughout. v6 includes Appendix 9.1; v4 ends after the references without an appendix.

before.justification: v4 reports original fine-tuning results, rank and operator ablations, and resource measurements in Tables 1–7 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v6 retains original fine-tuning and resource results and adds Mistral-7B evaluations and initial-gradient measurements in Table 2, Figure 1 and Appendix 9.1.

M1.justification: v4's general Bone and efficient Best Bone correspond to v6's DiSHA and Bone. Shared-matrix replication, summing inputs before multiplication, and Bat's blockwise weight-times-matrix-plus-matrix update remain operationally equivalent. The expanded framework description and nonlinear terminology do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five GLUE tasks, MetaMathQA/GSM8K/MATH, CodeFeedback/HumanEval, and WizardLM-Evol-Instruct/MT-Bench. Mistral-7B adds a model configuration on retained tasks. The gradient investigation does not identify additional datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. v6 Figure 1 adds FT, Frozen FT and BigLoRA as initial-gradient controls alongside LoRA and PiSSA. Conversely, the Bat-Hadamard comparator in v4 Section 4.6/Table 6 disappears.

E3.justification: v6 adds Mistral-7B configurations and an initial-gradient protocol spanning ranks 32–256, with BigLoRA fixed at rank 1024. Retained task splits, sample sizes and metrics are unchanged. Table 4 relabels RWKV6-3B as RWKV6-7B, matching the already-existing prose; this correction does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v6 introduces a controlled gradient investigation of initialization, parameter count and structural explanations for convergence (Figure 1 and Appendix 9.1). It removes the Hadamard-versus-matrix-multiplication investigation supporting Weight Guide (v4 Section 4.6). This substantially changes the mechanistic evidence, while the rank, Bone-versus-Bat and grouping analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds for GLUE and two for NLG, with unchanged averaging and uncertainty-reporting practices. The new gradient analysis supplies no additional run-count, confidence-interval or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: v6 adds Mistral-7B results and a distinct family of gradient findings, including BigLoRA's initial norm of 12.64. Bone scores 66.94/18.85/41.76 on Mistral GSM8K/MATH/HumanEval; PiSSA leads GSM8K at 67.01. v4's Hadamard results are removed. Bone's single-GPU throughput changes from 3.95 to 3.99 kt/s (v4 Table 7/v6 Table 6). Retained benchmark scores and loss curves otherwise match.

T1.justification: v6 explicitly formulates the two-dimensional DiSHA matrix D, its small-dimension condition and expansion map. The standalone Weight Guide and Hadamard formulations in v4 Equations 2 and 5 are removed. The operative Bone/Bat algebra remains equivalent, and neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v4 centers Bone and Weight Guide, with Bat validating pretrained-weight guidance. v6 centers DiSHA as a framework claimed to unlock lower intrinsic ranks and faster convergence by default, and presents Bat as producing nonlinear shard updates without additional parameters. Its contribution list also introduces an explicit SOTA claim.

C2.justification: v6 attributes slow convergence partly to LoRA's structure and interprets Bat's gains through nonlinear independence rather than Weight Guide's weight interactions. It newly acknowledges missing full-training results because of equipment limitations. Multimodal applicability changes from an open future-work question to a stated belief that the methods can handle any multimodal task.

D1.justification: v6 adds a Hugging Face PEFT access link alongside the renamed project address. Appendix 9.1 documents Frozen FT's zero-initialized full-size matrix and BigLoRA's rank-1024 construction. Most hardware and training disclosures remain unchanged; the new gradient experiment's model, data and norm-aggregation details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The central positioning shifts from GQA/MQA-inspired sharing and PiSSA-inspired Weight Guide to DiSHA as a general alternative addressing LoRA's structural limitations and initialization complexity. Related-work discussion emphasizes intrinsic rank and preprocessing overhead. Most cited literature remains, although the Touvron et al. Llama 2 and Wang–Kanwar bfloat16 references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, method narrative, conclusion and future-work section are extensively rewritten. DiSHA framework/design-space subsections replace the earlier motivation and Weight Guide organization, and acknowledgments and a gradient appendix are added. Much of the benchmark prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v6 adds gradient and partition diagrams, redraws the architecture and Bat illustrations, and removes v4's training-step schematic. Identical loss plots move to Figures 5 and 6. Tables are substantially compressed and rearranged, with Mistral rows added, the Hadamard table removed, and several displays placed beside wrapped text.

improvement.justification: v6 provides clearer shard explanations, additional Mistral results and gradient controls. However, it removes the operator ablation and promotes undefined nonlinear-independence claims although the displayed Bat updates remain linear in the trainable matrices for fixed weights. The gradient experiment is insufficiently specified, and retained across-the-board NLG superiority wording conflicts with the new Mistral GSM8K result. These empirical and presentation gains coexist with weakened mechanistic justification, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
